outputs.explanation: This is a scatter plot in which each of the 141 markers represents one individual sample measurement (rhythmicity index vs. period), so the raw individual data points are the plot itself. The marginal histograms further summarize the distribution of these individual measurements. Scatter plots showing raw points are exempt/self-satisfying for this check.

Although rendered with scatter-style markers, each point represents the mean ± s.d. across 6 (or 5, or 3) replicate samples per reporter/cell line, i.e. an aggregated average rather than an individual raw measurement. No individual replicate data points are overlaid to show the underlying spread, only summary error bars, so this does not qualify for the scatter-plot exemption and fails the check.

These are density/normal-distribution curves (a line-plot type) of subtype-averaged periods and amplitudes. Line/density plots are exempt from requiring overlaid individual data points, as such overlays would make the plot unreadable.

This is a box plot of CWT ridge lengths (25th/75th percentile boxes, whiskers, median lines, outliers marked). Box plots inherently convey the data distribution and are exempt from the individual-points requirement; the panel additionally already overlays per-sample dots (Per2-Luc/Bmal1-Luc) confirming the underlying data are visible.

This is a polar histogram displaying frequency/probability distributions of phase differences per cell line. Histogram-type plots are exempt from the individual-data-point overlay requirement, similar to other frequency-distribution plots.
This is a polar histogram of subtype-averaged phase differences. As a histogram/frequency-distribution plot, it is exempt from needing overlaid individual data points.

This panel shows a single illustrative example trace (original signal, fitted decaying sinusoid, and sketched decay envelope) used to explain the fitting method, not an average computed across multiple samples/replicates. No averaging is being summarized, so the individual-data-point requirement does not apply.

Each of the 117 markers represents one individual sample's fitted amplitude and decay rate, i.e., the raw individual measurements are plotted directly (error bars reflect fitting uncertainty for that single sample, not variability across replicates being averaged out). This satisfies the scatter-plot exemption since the points themselves are the individual data.
